items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: I knew about the book, a lot of so noted, like Gershwin for example, they studied with Joseph Schillinger.

ctx.x: F. Form F, that school has to approve, and the school would have to have that qualification. Not every little private school could do it. So things like that. And there was a guitar player from Boston that was drafted, and he told me about this school. In those days it was called Berklee School for Music and before that it used to be called Schillinger House. And I knew about the book, a lot of so noted, like Gershwin for example, they studied with Joseph Schillinger. So that’s what they were teaching. So I…

Norman Granz. And when I wrote the letter to the school that I wished to be accepted in the school, and that Norman Granz had written a big article about me simultaneously while he was releasing my record, it was a ten inch in those days, and the school noticed that, so they decided — it was a very small school at that time. So I think it works better for both of us that they gave me a full scholarship, the school got a lot of publicity because of that too. So that’s how I came to school in Boston. And then I…
